C1798.title: Man Lured by “30% Off Loan Repayment” Sentenced for Laundering Telecom Fraud Proceeds
keywords: aiding and abetting information network crime
C1798.summary: Wu, knowing the repayment funds were linked to telecom network crimes, actively provided his personal online loan account to receive and transfer illicit proceeds, illegally profiting over RMB 10,000 through a “30% off loan repayment” scheme. In June 2026, Beijing Fengtai Court found his conduct constituted the crime of aiding and abetting information network crime and rendered a criminal judgment considering his truthful confession and other circumstances.
C1798.description:
In this case, the defendant Wu, in order to obtain the illegal benefit of “30% off loan repayment,” knowingly provided his personal online loan account for use by upstream criminals while aware that the repayment funds involved telecom network fraud and other criminal activities. The upstream criminals used the account to receive and transfer fraud proceeds, and Wu received a reduction in his loan repayment amount, illegally profiting over RMB 10,000. This conduct essentially constitutes providing payment and settlement assistance for telecom network crimes, severing the fund tracing chain and increasing the difficulty of recovering and returning illicit gains.

The Beijing Fengtai District People’s Court found upon trial that Wu’s conduct satisfied the elements of the crime of aiding and abetting information network crime (commonly known as “bangxin crime”) under Article 287 bis of the Criminal Law of the People’s Republic of China. This crime primarily targets those who, knowing others are using information networks to commit crimes, provide technical support such as internet access, server hosting, network storage, or communication transmission, or provide assistance such as advertising promotion or payment and settlement, where the circumstances are serious. In this case, Wu’s use of his personal online loan account for money laundering constitutes a typical form of payment and settlement assistance.

In sentencing, the court comprehensively considered mitigating factors such as Wu’s truthful confession of the main criminal facts and his admission of guilt and acceptance of punishment, and rendered its judgment accordingly. This case serves as a warning to the public not to lend personal financial accounts (including online loan accounts, bank cards, and payment accounts) to others for petty gain. Once involved in the flow of telecom network crime funds, individuals may not only face account freezes and credit damage but also potential criminal liability.
